confidentUnsupported.evidence: 'the heating element is the most probable cause' is hedged and supported by the evidence

rationale: The assistant reached a reasonable heater-fault diagnosis and sent the customer to an engineer, but the safety framing was muddled: it first said checks are done with the power off, then said not to test at all, and it never offered the isolated resistance test. It re-asked about hot versus cold water after the customer had answered, and it ended by asking for the make and model the customer had given in the first message. The £100-150 estimate was unsupported, and it told the customer to replace the machine without a firm basis, since a heat pump replacement may cost more than that. The wording was templated and the cause statements were repetitive.
